Intravenous aldesleukin therapy was associated with varying degrees of acute renal dysfunction in al- most all of 99 adult patients.1 The clinical syndrome of hypoten- sion, oliguria, fluid retention, and associated azotaemia with in- tense tubular avidity for filtered sodium all support prerenal acute renal failure as the cause of renal dysfunction. However, renal function values returned to baseline levels within 7 days in 62% of patients and in 95% by 30 days.
